arxiv-2003-10619.title: Occurrence control of charged exciton for a single CdSe quantum dot at cryogenic temperatures on an optical nanofiber Journal: Applied Physics B
arxiv-2003-10619.creator: K. Muhammed Shafi, Kazunori Iida, Emi Tsutsumi, Akiharu Miyanaga, Kohzo Hakuta
arxiv-2003-10619.description: Abstract We discuss photo-luminescence characteristics of CdSe core/shell quantum dots at cryogenic temperatures using a hybrid system of a single quantum dot and an optical nanofiber. The key point is to control the emission species of quantum dot to charged excitons, known as trions, which have superior characteristics to neutral excitons.

arxiv-2101-02332.title: Identification of Latent Variables From Graphical Model Residuals
arxiv-2101-02332.creator: Boris Hayete, Fred Gruber, Anna Decker, Raymond Yan
arxiv-2101-02332.description: Abstract Graph-based causal discovery methods aim to capture conditional independencies consistent with the observed data and differentiate causal relationships from indirect or induced ones. Successful construction of graphical models of data depends on the assumption of causal sufficiency: that is, that all confounding variables are measured.

arxiv-2103-12612.title: Rigidity Percolation in Disordered 3D Rod Systems Thanks: This work was supported by the U.S. Army Research Office (#W911NF-13-1-0013 and #W911NF-16-1-0356), and by the National Science Foundation awards DMS-1664645 and CISE-1931516. Additional support was provided by a James S. McDonnell Foundation
arxiv-2103-12612.creator: Samuel Heroy, Dane Taylor, Feng Shi, M. Gregory Forest, Peter J. Mucha
arxiv-2103-12612.description: Abstract In composite materials composed of soft polymer matrix and stiff, high-aspect-ratio particles, the composite undergoes a transition in mechanical strength when the inclusion phase surpasses a critical density. This phenomenon (rheological or mechanical percolation) is well-known to occur in many composites at a critical density that exceeds the conductivity percolation threshold.

arxiv-2104-10617.title: Dynamical decoupling methods in nanoscale NMR
arxiv-2104-10617.creator: C. Munuera-Javaloy, R. Puebla, J. Casanova
arxiv-2104-10617.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by C. Munuera-Javaloy, R. Puebla, J. Casanova. Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) schemes can be applied to micron-, and nanometer-sized samples by the aid of quantum sensors such as nitrogen-vacancy (NV) color centers in diamond. These minute devices allow for magnetometry of nuclear spin ensembles with high spatial and frequency resolution at ambient conditions, thus having a clear impact in different areas such as chemistry, biology, medicine, and material sciences.

arxiv-2109-03775.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
arxiv-2109-03775.creator: Lan Zhang, Dapeng Wu, Xiaoyong Yuan
arxiv-2109-03775.description: Abstract Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices.

arxiv-2207-02728.title: Formalising Fisher’s Inequality: Formal Linear Algebraic Proof Techniques in Combinatorics
arxiv-2207-02728.creator: Chelsea Edmonds, Lawrence C. Paulson
arxiv-2207-02728.description: Abstract The formalisation of mathematics is continuing rapidly, however combinatorics continues to present challenges to formalisation efforts, such as its reliance on techniques from a wide range of other fields in mathematics. This paper presents formal linear algebraic techniques for proofs on incidence structures in Isabelle/HOL, and their application to the first formalisation of Fisher’s inequality.

arxiv-2207-09541.title: A Normal Test for Independence via Generalized Mutual Information Thanks: Department of Mathematics and Statistics, University of North Carolina at Charlotte
arxiv-2207-09541.creator: Jialin Zhang
arxiv-2207-09541.description: Abstract Testing hypothesis of independence between two random elements on a joint alphabet is a fundamental exercise in statistics. Pearson’s chi-squared test is an effective test for such a situation when the contingency table is relatively small. General statistical tools are lacking when the contingency data tables are large or sparse.

arxiv-2302-02504.title: Motion-compensated MR CINE reconstruction with reconstruction-driven motion estimation
arxiv-2302-02504.creator: Jiazhen Pan, Wenqi Huang, Daniel Rueckert, , Thomas Küstner, and Kerstin Hammernik
arxiv-2302-02504.description: Abstract In cardiac CINE, motion-compensated MR reconstruction (MCMR) is an effective approach to address highly undersampled acquisitions by incorporating motion information between frames. In this work, we propose a novel perspective for addressing the MCMR problem and a more integrated and efficient solution to the MCMR field.

arxiv-2306-04942.title: Momentum flux fluctuations in wall turbulence formulated along the distance from the wall Preprint: Physics of Fluids
arxiv-2306-04942.creator: Hideaki Mouri, Junshi Ito
arxiv-2306-04942.description: Abstract Wall turbulence has a sublayer where the mean wall-normal flux of the streamwise momentum is constant. Via the law of the wall, this mean flux is related to the wall-normal profile of the mean streamwise velocity. However, the momentum flux has large fluctuations, for which the corresponding law is yet unknown.

arxiv-2311-04865.title: Computing the 5 5 -Edge-Connected Components in Linear Time
arxiv-2311-04865.creator: Evangelos Kosinas
arxiv-2311-04865.description: Abstract We provide a deterministic algorithm for computing the 5 5 -edge-connected components of an undirected multigraph in linear time. There were probably good indications that this computation can be performed in linear time, but no such algorithm was actually known prior to this work.

arxiv-2410-22324.title: Perceptions of Blind Adults on Non-Visual Mobile Text Entry Conference: The PErvasive Technologies Related to Assistive Environments; June 25–27, 2025; Corfu Island, Greece The PErvasive Technologies Related to Assistive Environments (PETRA ’25), June 25–27, 2025, Corfu Island, Greece DOI: 10.1145/3
arxiv-2410-22324.creator: Dylan Gaines, Keith Vertanen
arxiv-2410-22324.description: Abstract . Text input on mobile devices without physical keys can be challenging for people who are blind or low-vision. We interview 12 blind adults about their experiences with current mobile text input to provide insights into what sorts of interface improvements may be the most beneficial.

arxiv-2512-14252.title: Gödel’s Poetry
arxiv-2512-14252.creator: Kelly J. Davis
arxiv-2512-14252.description: Abstract Formal, automated theorem proving has long been viewed as a challenge to artificial intelligence. We introduce here a new approach to computer theorem proving, one that employs specialized language models for Lean4 proof generation combined with recursive decomposition of difficult theorems into simpler entailing propositions.

arxiv-2602-08727.title: Artifact Reduction in Undersampled 3D Cone-Beam CTs using a Hybrid 2D-3D CNN Framework
arxiv-2602-08727.creator: Johannes Thalhammer ∗ 1 − 4 {{*1-4}} ✉, Tina Dorosti ∗ 1 − 3 {{*1-3}}, Sebastian Peterhansl 1 , 2 {{1,2}}, Daniela Pfeiffer 3 , 4 {{3,4}}, Franz Pfeiffer 1 − 4 {{1-4}}, Florian Schaff 1 , 2 {{1,2}}
arxiv-2602-08727.description: Abstract Undersampled CT volumes minimize acquisition time and radiation exposure but introduce artifacts degrading image quality and diagnostic utility. Reducing these artifacts is critical for high-quality imaging. We propose a computationally efficient hybrid deep-learning framework that combines the strengths of 2D and 3D models. First, a 2D U-Net operates on individual slices of undersampled CT volumes to extract feature maps.

pmc-10503318.title: Characteristics of programmes designed to link community-dwelling older adults in high-income countries from community to clinical sectors: a scoping review protocol
pmc-10503318.creator: Miriam Gofine, Gregory Laynor, Antoinette Schoenthaler
pmc-10503318.description: IntroductionResearch on effectively navigating older adults into primary care is urgently needed. Community–clinic linkage models (CCLMs) aim to improve population health by linking the health and community sectors in order to improve patients’ access to healthcare and, ultimately, population health. However, research on community-based points of entry linking adults with untreated medical needs into the healthcare sector is nascent.

pmc-10694175.title: Dual solutions of mixed convective hybrid nanofluid flow over a shrinking cylinder placed in a porous medium
pmc-10694175.creator: Nepal Chandra Roy, Aysha Akter
pmc-10694175.description: Mixed convective hybrid nanofluid flow over a shrinking cylinder saturated in a porous medium is analyzed in the presence of magnetic field. The mathematical model of the present problem is formulated with constant thermophysical properties. The system of governing equations is reduced to ordinary differential equations utilizing appropriate similarity transformations.

pmc-10701945.title: Mind-mindedness and styles of interaction of young fathers with their infants at three months: a pilot study
pmc-10701945.creator: Elena Ierardi, Simona Fantoni, Margherita Moioli, Alessandro Albizzati, Cristina Riva Crugnola
pmc-10701945.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundFatherhood at a young age can be characterized by a multiproblematic background with several risk factors that can negatively affect father-child relationships, the father’s well-being and child’s social-emotional development.MethodsThis pilot study evaluated paternal interaction styles and mentalization in a sample of 22 young fathers and their 3-month-old infants and compared these variables with those of 22 adolescent and young mothers (the fathers’ partners).

pmc-10712035.title: Reproductive decision making in women with medical comorbidities: a qualitative study
pmc-10712035.creator: Elena M. Kraus, Niraj R. Chavan, Victoria Whelan, Jennifer Goldkamp, James M. DuBois
pmc-10712035.description: BackgroundA growing number of reproductive-age women in the U.S. have chronic medical conditions, increasing their risk of perinatal morbidity and mortality. Still, they experience unintended pregnancies at similar rates to low-risk mothers. We have limited understanding of how these individuals consider decisions about pregnancy and contraceptive use.

pmc-11271935.title: Meta-analysis of the accuracy for RASSF1A methylation in bronchial aspirates for the diagnosis of lung cancer
pmc-11271935.creator: Xu-ping Chen, Shi-xu He, Meng-you Chen, Fu-bin Chen, Peng Wu, Ping Shi, Shi-cai Zhao, Ling-yan Zhao, Xiao-min Xiong, Jia Zeng
pmc-11271935.description: ObjectiveTo establish the diagnostic accuracy of RASSF1A (Ras association domain family 1 isoform) methylation using bronchial aspirates as an auxiliary method for diagnosing lung cancer through a systematic review and meta-analysis.MethodsStudies published prior to October 30, 2022, were retrieved from the Embase, PubMed, Web of Science, and Wan Fang databases using the keywords “lung cancer”, “RASSF1A”, “methylation”, and “bronchial aspirates”.

pmc-11348550.title: Assessment of SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complex related genes as potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets in pan-cancer
pmc-11348550.creator: Kai Zhuang, Lishan Wang, Chengyu Lu, Zhiping Liu, Dongli Yang, Hao Zhong, Jiami Zou, Aamir Fahira, Jiaojiao Wang, Zunnan Huang
pmc-11348550.description: Recent research has uncovered a surprisingly high occurrence of aberrant expression and mutations in the genes that encode subunits of the SWI/SNF chromatin-remodeling complexes (SCRC). Nevertheless, the carcinogenic effects of aberrant expression and mutations in SWI/SNF genes have only been acknowledged in recent times, resulting in a comparatively limited understanding of these modifications.

pmc-11532823.title: Slow but flexible or fast but rigid? Discrete and continuous processes compared
pmc-11532823.creator: Matteo Priorelli, Ivilin Peev Stoianov
pmc-11532823.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). A tradeoff exists when dealing with complex tasks composed of multiple steps. High-level cognitive processes can find the best sequence of actions to achieve a goal in uncertain environments, but they are slow and require significant computational demand. In contrast, lower-level processing allows reacting to environmental stimuli rapidly, but with limited capacity to determine optimal actions or to replan when expectations are not met.

pmc-11590607.title: Immunogenicity and protective efficacy of an inactivated infectious bronchitis virus vaccine candidate from a local isolate of Bangladesh
pmc-11590607.creator: Mst. Kohinoor Parvin, Md. Enamul Haque, Mohammad Aynul Haque, Md. Mostofa Kamal, Mohammad Sadekuzzaman, Sajedul Hayat, Md. Tanvir Rahman, Mahbubul Pratik Siddique, Sham Soun Nahar, A. K. M. Khasruzzaman, Muhammad Tofazzal Hossain, Md. Alimul Islam
pmc-11590607.description: Objective:Infectious bronchitis (IB), a highly infectious acute viral disease, is a major burden to the chicken industry worldwide. The research aimed to develop an inactivated IB vaccine using local isolates and assess its immunogenicity compared to other commercial live IB vaccines.Materials and Methods:An inactivated vaccine using a candidate IB virus (PP067159.

pmc-12609625.title: Primary PreserFlo MicroShunt Versus Trabeculectomy: Effectiveness and Safety in the Real World
pmc-12609625.creator: Anoushka N Kothari, Graham A Lee, Etsuo Chihara, Esther M Hoffmann, Tina Tzee Ling Wong
pmc-12609625.description: Backgrounds/Objectives: Trabeculectomy is the gold standard for glaucoma drainage surgery, but it is associated with a risk of sight-threatening complications. The PreserFlo MicroShunt (PF) is a less invasive alternative that aims to reduce complications and simplify post-operative care. This study aimed to compare the effectiveness and safety of PF to trabeculectomy in the management of glaucoma.

pmc-12630517.title: A Journey to Childhood for Therapeutic Purposes: Utilizing Gamification for the Rehabilitation of Stroke Patients
pmc-12630517.creator: Reza Abdollahi, Mir Hossein Ahmadi
pmc-12630517.description: litation program and are unable to motivate them. To address this issue, the use of innovative rehabilitation approaches such as gamification can be employed (1). Gamification, defined as the application of game elements in non-game contexts, is used with the aim of incorporating aspects such as rewards, challenges, and interactive feedback into rehabilitation programs.

pmc-12802789.title: Does altitude have an effect on stroke mortality and hospitalization risk? A comprehensive evaluation of United States data
pmc-12802789.creator: Jacob Gerken, Nathan Huber, Demi Zapata, Ileana G. Barron, Isain Zapata
pmc-12802789.description: BackgroundGlobally, stroke is a leading cause of death among people over 50 years of age. In the United States alone, over 150,000 people die due to stroke every year. Environmental factors such as altitude may play a role in these outcomes; however, their effects have not yet been comprehensively explored.

pmc-13137181.title: Viscous drag-induced self-regeneration of laser-dissected actin stress fibers: A potential mechanism for mechanical memory
pmc-13137181.creator: Kazuaki Nagayama
pmc-13137181.description: Biological tissues are constantly subjected to physiological mechanical stresses that can induce microdamage to cellular components, a process linked to cellular aging and carcinogenesis. Actin stress fibers (SFs) are central to maintaining structural integrity and transducing mechanical cues to intracellular organelles.

pmc-13214446.title: DNA polymerase characteristics influence noise levels in sequencing of short tandem repeats
pmc-13214446.creator: Tova Lindh, Maja Sidstedt, Kevin M Kiesler, Peter M Vallone, Johannes Hedman
pmc-13214446.description: BackgroundPolymerase chain reaction (PCR) applications including sequencing rely on thermostable DNA polymerases and their ability to generate accurate amplicons. Polymerization errors may hinder the detection of low-level DNA variants such as mutations in clinical samples or DNA from minor contributors in crime scene traces with DNA from multiple individuals.
